latest_substantive_result.summary: The selected 0457 source states a one-sided actual-instrument selection theorem that charges the conditional classical question-law drift and quantum state change jointly. For a finite game with bounded payoff, m iid question pairs, an actual Alice-only success sub-POVM, Bob's original complete full-string POVM untouched, and a referee channel with common component δ>0, it constructs a legal same-model base strategy with β≤(√α+√(ln(1/p)/(δm)))² and the corresponding game-gap exponential bound. When α≤ε it also gives an exact binary-affinity consequence. Finite-tensor and unrestricted commuting base values remain distinct. Earlier weaker selector sources remain unchanged; general Bob-dependent selection, efficient acquisition, finite commuting representation, physical performance and external novelty are not established.

publication.scope: Finite two-player game G with V∈[0,1], one-round law μ(x,y), m≥1 iid question PAIRS, arbitrary full-string joint local measurements, and an input-independent shared resource. Selection is an actual Alice success sub-POVM event E depending on her full question string and instrument outcome/steering, never Bob's input or outcome; Bob's original full-string complete POVM is untouched. Let p=Pr(E)>0 and α be the selected conditional expected fraction of coordinate losses. Require μ(y|x)=δν(y)+(1−δ)κ(y|x) on positive-marginal x, 0<δ≤1; the reset flag is not exposed. The same-model constructed loss β satisfies β≤(√α+√τ)², ε≤(√α+√τ)², τ=ln(1/p)/(δm), hence p≤exp(−δm(√ε−√α)_+²). For α≤ε the exact affinity bound is ln(1/p)/(δm)≥−2ln(√(αε)+√((1−α)(1−ε))); at α=0, p≤(1−ε)^(δm)=ω_model(G)^(δm). Here ε=1−ω_* for finite tensor and ε_co=1−ω_co for unrestricted commuting, with no identification between them. Free inputs have δ=1. The commuting construction uses one common standard form and may be infinite-dimensional. The finite-dimensional construction has at most d_B quantum dimension per offline branch but potentially exponentially many branches.
